title: Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) Pretreatment Protocols for Bone Material
author: Samantha Brown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf5djq26

steps.title: Prepare Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the following solutions in a fume hood. Label all bottles with the solution name, concentration, preparer's name, and date.

substeps.instruction: 0.6 M HCl: Add 50 ml of 37% HCl (~12 M) to 950 ml ultrapure water OR 100 ml of 20% HCl (~6 M) to 900 ml ultrapure water. Mix by gently inverting. Store at 4°C.
0.1 M NaOH: Dissolve 4g of stock NaOH pellets (~2 pellets) in 1000 ml ultrapure water. Mix by gently inverting. Store at 4°C.

50 mM Ammonium Bicarbonate (AmBic) buffer, pH 8: Weigh 3.95 g of AmBic powder into a clean glass bottle, fill to 1000 ml, and mix by gently inverting. Adjust pH by adding droplets of 1 M AmBic if necessary. Store at 4°C.
5% Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA): Dilute 1 ml TFA stock solution in 19 ml water in a brown glass bottle. Mix by gently inverting. Store for 6 months.
Wash solution (0.1% TFA in ultrapure water): Add 1000 µl of TFA stock solution to 1000 ml of ultrapure water. Mix by gently inverting. Store at room temperature.
Conditioning solution (0.1% TFA in 50% ACN): Mix 500 ml ACN with 500 ml ultrapure water, then carefully add 1000 µl of TFA. Store at room temperature in a bottle with minimal headspace.
Trypsin solution (0.4 µg/µl): Resuspend freeze-dried Trypsin in 50 µl of Trypsin resuspension buffer. Transfer to a 0.5 ml tube and store at -20°C.

steps.title: Weigh Bone Samples
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of bone into a labeled microcentrifuge tube and record the weight.

substeps.instruction: Archaeological samples: 10-20 mg bone chips or ~10 mg bone powder.
Modern samples: 5-15 mg bone chips or ~7 mg bone powder.

steps.title: Perform Non-destructive Collagen Extraction (Section A)
steps.instruction: Extract collagen using the buffer method if non-destructive analysis is required.

substeps.instruction: Pretreatment: Add 100 µL of 50 mM AmBic (or enough to cover the sample). Leave at ambient temperature overnight (up to a week). Centrifuge at high speed for 1 min and discard supernatant.
Gelatinization: Add 100 µL of AmBic (use 50 µL for limited samples, or more to cover large samples). Incubate for 1 hour at 65°C.

Collection: Centrifuge for 1 min. Transfer 50 µL of supernatant to a tube labeled 'EXT' and the remaining 50 µL to a tube labeled 'SE'. If volume exceeds 200 µL, reduce by evaporation (heat block or vacuum centrifuge) to 100-200 µL before splitting.

steps.title: Perform Destructive Acid Demineralization (Section B/C)
steps.instruction: Demineralize bone using HCl for acid-insoluble or acid-soluble fraction analysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of cold (4°C) 0.6 M HCl (or enough to cover sample). Store in fridge at 4°C until demineralization is complete (bone is flexible/spongy, no bubbling). Bone powders typically take 4-10h; others 1 day to 2 weeks.
Centrifuge for 1 min. Remove the acid supernatant into a tube labeled 'AC' and store at -20°C (this is the acid-soluble fraction for Section C).

steps.title: Process Acid Insoluble Collagen (Section B continued)
steps.instruction: Clean and gelatinize the bone chip/powder fraction remaining after demineralization.

substeps.instruction: Wash: Add 200 µL of 50 mM AmBic, mix, centrifuge, and discard. Repeat 3 times.
Humic Acid Removal: Add 200 µL of 0.1 M NaOH, mix, incubate for 5 min, centrifuge, and discard NaOH wash.
Neutralize: Add 200 µL of 50 mM AmBic, mix, centrifuge, and discard. Repeat 3 times.
Gelatinization: Add 100 µL of AmBic (use 50 µL for limited samples, or more to cover large samples). Incubate for 1 hour at 65°C.

Collection: Centrifuge at 20,000 rpm (or highest speed) for 1 min. Transfer 50 µL of supernatant to 'EXT' tube and remaining 50 µL to 'SE' tube. If volume exceeds 200 µL, reduce by evaporation to 100-200 µL before splitting.

steps.title: Process Acid Soluble Collagen (Section C continued)
steps.instruction: Perform buffer exchange on the 'AC' supernatant using ultrafilters.

substeps.instruction: Place 250 µL of acid supernatant into a 30 kDa ultrafilter (use 3 kDa or 10 kDa for poorly preserved collagen).
Centrifuge at 3700 rpm until acid is pushed through (5-30 min). Discard flow-through.
Add 500 µL of 50 mM AmBic, centrifuge at 3700 rpm, and discard flow-through.
Elution: Add 100 µL of 50 mM AmBic (use 50 µL for limited samples) to the filter and mix by pipetting.
Collection: Transfer 50 µL of supernatant to 'EXT' tube and remaining 50 µL to 'SE' tube. Discard filter.

steps.title: Digest Proteins with Trypsin
steps.instruction: Perform enzymatic digestion on the 'EXT' sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL of trypsin solution (0.4 µg/µl) to the 'EXT' tube.
Incubate overnight at 37°C (approx. 12-18 h).
Centrifuge for 1 min and add 1 µL of 5% TFA to stop the reaction.

steps.title: Purify Peptides via C18 ZipTip
steps.instruction: Purify the digested peptides using C18 ZipTips. Use a pipette set to 100 µL throughout.

substeps.instruction: Prepare tubes: 'C' (250 µL Conditioning Solution), 'W' (450 µL Washing Solution), and 'COL' (50 µL Conditioning Solution).
Condition Tip: Rinse the C18 tip twice with 100 µL of conditioning solution and discard.
Wash Tip: Rinse the tip twice with 100 µL of wash solution and discard.
Bind Sample: Resuspend the 'EXT' sample back and forth over the tip at least 5 times (do not push air through the filter).
Final Wash: Rinse the tip twice with 100 µL of wash solution and discard.
Elution: Elute the sample into the 'COL' tube using the 50 µL of conditioning solution, passing through the tip at least 5 times.
